results.content: MicroMix: Efficient Mixed-Precision Quantization with Microscaling Formats for Large Language Models. To bridge this gap, we propose MicroMix, a co-designed mixed-precision quantization algorithm and matrix multiplication kernel based on Microscaling (MX) data formats. To achieve a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency for each linear layer, we introduce quantization thresholds that identify activation elements where lower-precision formats (MXFP4 or MXFP6) incur excessive quantization error. Quantization has emerged as a critical technique for accelerating inference in large language models (LLMs), reducing both computational cost and memory footprint by replacing high-precision (e.g., FP16) operations with lower-precision counterparts. MicroMix addresses this gap by introducing a co-designed mixed-precision quantization algorithm and kernel based on Microscaling (MX) data formats—specifically MXFP4, MXFP6, and MXFP8. By integrating quantization, reordering, and matrix multiplication into a fused kernel, MicroMix minimizes overhead and maximizes efficiency on Blackwell GPUs. Figure 1: Overview of MicroMix.
